པ་ཞེས་བྱ་བའི་ཚིག་གསུམ་པོ་འདིས་ནི་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་དེ་སེམས་ཅན་གང་དག་ལ་བརྟེན་ནས་སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་དོན་མཛད་པ་དེ་སྟོན་པར་བྱེད་དེ། སེམས་ཅན་དེ་དག་ཀྱང་དད་པའི་བསམ་པའམ། ཟིལ་གྱིས་མནན་པའི་བསམ་པ་སྟེ། བསམ་པ་གཉིས་ཀྱིས་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པའི་དྲུང་དུ་འོང་ངོ་། །

Merely by seeing him, one realizes, "This is a Great Being," and generates great faith. This very thing is what is meant by "nothing about him is discordant to behold."

"The delight of those who are devoted with faith; not overwhelmed by wisdom; and not trampled by strengths" — these three phrases show which beings the Blessed One relies upon to perform the welfare of beings. Those beings come before the Tathagata with two types of intentions: either an intention of faith or an intention to overwhelm him. 

The intention of faith is also of two kinds: the intention of wondering "what is he like?" or the intention of great joy. Because both are of the nature of aspiration, they are called "faith." In this way, some develop the intention of wondering what he is like, and being truly exhorted by previous roots of virtue, they go before the Tathagata. Others, having heard of his great virtuous qualities, develop genuine faith, and being exhorted by roots of virtue, they go. Therefore, this shows both those who are neutral and those who have faith. Because he makes them feel joy and develop great faith upon seeing him, the Blessed One is the cause of delight for both those types of devoted people.

The intention to overwhelm is also of two kinds. The intention to overwhelm with wisdom is, for example, like the Truth-Tellers <note>Satyakas</note> who seek debate. The intention to overwhelm with physical strength is, for example, like the forest-dwellers and others who are arrogant regarding their strength. Therefore, this truly shows those who are hostile with these two types of intentions. Because the Blessed One possesses transcendent wisdom and possesses transcendent activity that overwhelms others, he is not overwhelmed by the wisdom of those who wish to overwhelm him, and he is not trampled by their strengths.

"The teacher of all beings; the father of
tail: Bodhisattvas; the king of noble individuals; the caravan leader for those traveling to the city of Nirvana" — these four phrases show the Blessed One's performance of whatever activities are necessary for all sentient beings.

"The great joy of those who are resolved with faith," "Unconquerable by wisdom," "Inviolable by powers"—these three phrases show those beings upon whom the Blessed One relies to perform the benefit of beings. 
Those beings approach the presence of the Tathagata with either a thought of faith or a thought of attempting to outshine him.

Some, having heard of his Great Qualities of the Self, produce genuine great faith and, urged by their roots of virtue, they go. Therefore, this indicates those who dwell in the middle and those with faith. 
Because he causes them to feel joy and great faith upon seeing him, the Blessed One is the cause of great joy for both types of those resolved with faith.

and the thought of outshining him with physical strength, such as the forest-dwellers and others who are arrogant regarding their strength.
